leading_positions.synthesis: All eight round-1 configurations are a single prize part for B022 (optical lattice clocks) with the same two laureates, Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye. Several members (Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson) state that they moved to B022 after reading the other opening ballots, from B018, B011 and B038 respectively as their opening first choices; Pearce moved from B002. What is shared: the magic-wavelength idea, 10^-18 control of systematics, reproduction across several laboratories, and a two-name credit that most members call the cleanest on the shortlist. What is not fully shared: the citation wording (five members write 'invention' or 'invention and development/realisation', Danielsson and Mehlig write 'the optical lattice clock and its development' and add a forward-looking phrase on new precision tests or a new regime, Johansson centres on the path from the magic-wavelength concept to 10^-18, Olsson names magic-wavelength trapping explicitly), the weight given to Katori's concept versus Ye's record performance, and whether this is a discovery or a measurement tool. No member's round-1 configuration contains a second prize part, so there is no explicit minority configuration; minority views appear only in the alternatives and in objections.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members explicitly prefer B022 with Katori and Ye as the only configuration, and each states that no specific conflict bears on it (Kroll adds a mild personal-link disclosure, below).

Members describe the same mechanism: magic-wavelength trapping cancels the light shift between the clock states while the lattice removes Doppler and recoil effects, so many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once.
Members cite independent reproduction and clock-to-clock agreement at about the 10^-18 level at JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE and NIST, and on that basis call the result mature.

Members cite concrete science already delivered or in reach: millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, limits on varying constants and ultralight dark matter, relativistic geodesy, and a many-body (Fermi-degenerate) clock regime.
Members treat the Katori and Ye pairing as a defensible split, with Katori credited for the concept and first demonstrations and Ye for taking it to the record regime.

Members who opened elsewhere (the IceCube, DMFT, hexatic-melting and tunnel-magnetoresistance entries) say that attribution gaps or maturity questions in those entries, not lack of interest, keep them off the preferred configuration.
scientific_disputes: Discovery versus tool: every member raises the point that B022 is a precision-measurement advance whose largest scientific returns (dark matter, varying constants, relativity tests) are still mostly upper limits and consistency checks, with no new effect observed (Pearce, Kroll, Eriksson). Danielsson, Lindroth and Mehlig argue it is a clue extracted from nature by measurement; Eriksson and Pearce concede it is not a new state of matter or phenomenon.

Distinctness from earlier prizes: all eight flag the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize. Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Mehlig and Pearce argue the lattice architecture (many neutral atoms at the magic wavelength) is a different route to precision that a citation can separate from those prizes. Eriksson, Lindroth and Olsson keep it as an open worry that it reads as the next increment in one lineage.

Alternatives differ in kind: B020 (cold-atom quantum simulation) is the most-named fallback and is described as conceptually richer; B028 (moire flat bands) is preferred by Danielsson and Eriksson as a condensed-matter surprise, with Eriksson noting the unsettled pairing mechanism; B043 and B004 are cited as measurement-driven fallbacks. Members disagree on whether the fallback should be a quantum-simulation, a moire or a sensing entry, and none has been argued through to a configuration.

B002 (high-energy neutrinos): the diffuse flux is accepted as solid, but Danielsson, Johansson and Kroll view the source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) as still at modest significance; Pearce, who opened with it first, did not defend it as ready this year.
attribution_disputes: Credit around B022 beyond Katori and Ye: Lemonde and the SYRTE group, Gill, Hollberg, Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom and the ion-clock and comb groups are named by various members as contributors. No member proposes widening the configuration, and Lindroth explicitly resists widening it, but Danielsson, Kroll, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce state that they cannot verify priority from the packet.

Katori's priority versus the JILA record-setting performance: Lindroth notes that the weighting between concept and 10^-18 performance has to be settled; Pearce notes Ye's share is partly the work of a large JILA team.
B018: Metzner is absent from the credited trio (Eriksson, Danielsson, Pearce), and Mehlig and Danielsson call dynamical mean-field theory an approximation scheme more than a discovery.
B038: Yuasa and Djayaprawira are not credited for the MgO giant-TMR result (Olsson, Danielsson, Pearce), and the 1995 effect overlaps with the 2007 giant-magnetoresistance prize.

B002: a single credited name for a large collaboration and its AMANDA predecessor is called hard to defend by Johansson, Kroll, Danielsson and by Pearce himself, who named it as a reason he moved it down.
B004: Steven Chu is not among the supplied names (Kroll, Danielsson), and four names for three places leaves out someone such as Schmiedmayer.
B020: the decisive names are not settled. Danielsson, Johansson and Lindroth propose Bloch, Greiner and Zoller, Kroll adds Esslinger, and the pool of credited names has five.
maturity_disputes: The SI redefinition of the second has not happened. Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce list it as pending societal endorsement, and Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth ask explicitly whether the committee prefers to wait for it. Mehlig and Olsson judge the maturity of the scientific result sufficient without it.
Several alternatives are described as not yet ready: B002 on source significance, B028 on the unsettled pairing mechanism (Eriksson), B004 on prospective fundamental-physics reach (Danielsson).
B011 has thin support (two ranked members at opening), and Mehlig notes the 2016 Kosterlitz-Thouless prize makes it look like a late sequel and that KTHNY melting is not universal in practice.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Kroll: spent a year in John Hall's laboratory during his PhD, and Jun Ye is a long-standing close collaborator of Hall, so he discloses a mild personal link to the B022 community; he states he has no direct collaboration or supervisory tie to Katori or Ye and leaves it to the committee to judge.
Kroll: in the leadership of WACQT and would recuse from any decision that depends on B014 (circuit QED).

Johansson: director of WACQT, a theorist in superconducting circuits and a colleague of Chalmers groups (Delsing, Wilson); he would recuse himself from deliberation and voting on B014. He states this is not connected to B022, B020 or B043.

Pearce (chair): works in the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations, and discloses field closeness to B002 (IceCube) and B009 (kilonovae), with no known tie to IceCube or its credited candidate; no conflict for B022.
Lindroth: professionally close to atomic, molecular and optical physics as a subfield, but states this is shared closeness and not a personal tie, with no recusal issue for B020, B004 or B006.
Olsson and Johansson are Chalmers colleagues and Mehlig is in the Gothenburg environment, which members note without finding any bearing on B022.
questions_for_round2: Does the committee judge the lattice clock distinct enough from the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes to be written into a citation, and which wording (invention of the lattice clock, development to 10^-18, or both) would the members who prefer 'invention' and those who prefer 'development' each accept?

Is Katori and Ye the right and complete credit, or does any member insist on adding or substituting a name such as Lemonde, Gill or another early lattice-clock contributor? If so, on what primary evidence, and which of the three places would it use?
Should the committee wait for the redefinition of the second, or is demonstrated 10^-18 reproduction across laboratories sufficient maturity now?

Given that no round-1 configuration has a second part, does any member now propose one, and if so can B020 be reduced to a defensible set of names (Bloch, Greiner, Zoller, with or without Esslinger or Cirac) or is B028, B043 or B004 better placed?

Can members who raised the discovery-versus-tool objection (Eriksson, Kroll, Pearce) state what content in the citation would answer it, such as the gravitational-redshift and many-body results already demonstrated?

Does the committee regard Kroll's disclosed link through John Hall as requiring any step beyond disclosure, and do members who ranked B014 wish to confirm that Kroll's and Johansson's recusals on it are the only ones needed?
summary.chair_observation: All eight members converge on B022 with Katori and Ye as the only prize part, and the written objections are largely the same across members: closeness to the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes, uncredited contributors, a pending redefinition of the second, and the discovery-versus-instrument question. The disagreement that remains is mostly about citation wording, whether to add a second part, and which fallback to hold in reserve. The chair has counted only the positions written in the eight round-1 files.
